references.text: The Lord had already given instructions to gather manna, and the people's disobedience in verse 28 refers back to these original commands.
Earlier in the same chapter, the people refused to obey Moses' command not to keep any manna until the next day, showing a pattern of disobedience.
God asks how long the people will despise Him and refuse to believe, using the same type of rhetorical question about ongoing disobedience.
The Lord asks how long the people will refuse to humble themselves, using similar language about persistent resistance to God's will.
The psalm describes how Israel did not keep God's covenant and refused to walk in His law, summarizing the disobedience mentioned in Exodus.
The psalm states that they tested and rebelled against the Most High God and did not keep His testimonies.
Ezekiel describes Israel's repeated rebellion against God in the wilderness and their contempt for His laws and commands.
Jesus laments over Jerusalem, which repeatedly rejected God's messengers, echoing the same theme of persistent disobedience to God's will.
